cards.statement: In a non-defining clause, the relative pronoun can be replaced by a full repeated noun phrase without changing the structure.
cards.explanation: The relative pronoun is part of the clause structure.

cards.statement: Whose introduces a place rather than a possessive relationship.
Non-defining relative clauses are useful when a report needs to add context without changing the main reference.
cards.explanation: They add compact background information to an identified noun.

cards.statement: The phrase “the framework, within that the study operates” is formal and correct.
cards.explanation: Use within which, not within that.

cards.statement: In careful written English, that is normally interchangeable with which after a comma.
cards.explanation: That is avoided in non-defining clauses.

activities.explanation: Cada carta repasa una regla del tema; revisa las falladas al terminar el mazo.

activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 6 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: A comma before the relative clause can signal that the antecedent is already identified.
cards.explanation: That is the central discourse function of the construction.

cards.statement: The sentence “The museum, where it opened in 1890, is popular” is the clearest standard form.
cards.explanation: Use which opened; where is for a place relation and it repeats the subject.

cards.statement: Whose must be followed by a noun such as proposal, team or brother.
cards.explanation: Whose is a determiner expressing possession.

cards.statement: Who can refer to an identified person in an additional clause.
cards.explanation: Who is the usual relative pronoun for people.

cards.statement: The clause “whose proposal won” identifies the owner of the proposal.
cards.explanation: Whose connects the antecedent with the possessed noun.

cards.statement: Where and when are chosen mainly from the type of antecedent: place or time.
cards.explanation: Their selection depends on the semantic relation.

activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 7 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: In a non-defining clause, the relative pronoun can normally be omitted when it is the object.
cards.explanation: The pronoun remains explicit in this construction.

cards.statement: Where can introduce extra information about a place.
cards.explanation: Where links the clause to a location.

cards.statement: Under which is a possible formal phrase for a policy or framework.
cards.explanation: A preposition can come before which in formal writing.

cards.statement: The commas in “Dr Patel, who designed the survey, won” present the detail as additional.
cards.explanation: The name already identifies Dr Patel.

cards.statement: A defining clause and a non-defining clause always have identical meanings.
cards.explanation: Commas can change whether the information identifies the group.

cards.statement: On which can introduce an additional clause referring to a date.
cards.explanation: On which is a formal time-relative phrase.

cards.statement: In “The museum, which opened in 1890, is popular”, which is the subject of opened.
cards.explanation: No extra it is needed because which is the subject.
